subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

The philosopher's reluctance to endorse a universal ethic (1)/ stem from his conviction (2)/ that moral principles are always mediated (3)/ by cultural and historical particularities. (4)
solution:
The error is in part (2): “stem” should be “stems”.

The subject is the singular “reluctance” (to endorse a universal ethic); a singular subject takes a singular verb.

Correct sentence: The philosopher's reluctance to endorse a universal ethic stems from his conviction that moral principles are always mediated by cultural and historical particularities.
conceptTested: Subject-Verb Agreement: The verb must agree in number with the actual singular head noun, ignoring intervening prepositional phrases.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

Language, in its performative function, (1)/ shape the very ontology (2)/ of social relations and categories (3)/ that structure human perception. (4)
solution:
The error is in part (2): “shape” should be “shapes”.

The subject is the singular “Language” (the phrase “in its performative function” is only a modifier); a singular subject takes a singular verb.

Correct sentence: Language, in its performative function, shapes the very ontology of social relations and categories that structure human perception.
conceptTested: Subject-Verb Agreement: A singular subject separated from its verb by modifiers still requires a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

The philosopher's idea (1)/ that reality is constructed through language, (2)/ was refuted not by logic (3)/ but emotion and intuition. (4)
solution:
The error is in part (4): the correlative “not by logic ... but” must be completed with “by”, i.e. “but by emotion and intuition”.

The second limb of “not ... but” must repeat the preposition “by” for parallelism.

Correct sentence: The philosopher's idea that reality is constructed through language was refuted not by logic but by emotion and intuition.
conceptTested: Parallelism: Correlative conjunctions like \u2018not ... but\u201d must be followed by parallel grammatical structures (including preposition repetition).

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

Not only each participant's response (1)/ but also their metadata (2)/ was collected (3)/ and cross-validated. (4)
solution:
According to the official answer key, the error is considered to be in part (3) where “was collected” should be “were collected” based on proximity or collective plural agreement.

Corrected sentence: Not only each participant's response but also their metadata were collected and cross - validated.
conceptTested: Subject-Verb Agreement and Correlative Conjunctions: When subjects are joined by \u2018not only ... but also\u201d, the verb agrees with the closer subject.
